summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for his 26th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He presented electively in stable condition and received methotrexate 8 g/m² with urinary alkalinization. Temozolomide was continued on a 7-day on/7-day off cycle. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion, and methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.17. He tolerated treatment without complications. Hyponatremia did not develop, and potassium was managed with oral supplementation. Blood pressure was lower than baseline, prompting temporary hold of lisinopril. The patient reported persistent mild depressive symptoms; a plan to switch from Keppra to Depakote for potential mood benefit was discussed but deferred to outpatient follow-up. He was discharged home with instructions to resume all home medications and continue follow-up for Rituxan and MRI surveillance.
